Rugged tablet for Powered Now

Powered Now is job management software for UK trades. Its App Store listing describes creating certificates and forms on the go, including gas and electrical certificates, capturing customer signatures and recording hours against appointments. The vendor's own site lists quotes, invoices, job notes and photos, and says the software works across iOS, Android, Mac and Windows with data syncing between devices.

For an electrician or other tradesperson, the app is where the certificate, the customer signature and the job photos are completed, often in a loft, a plant room or a new-build with no signal. That means a device that is handled with dusty hands, carried in and out of a van and sometimes dropped, which is where a consumer tablet in a slim case tends to give up.

This page sets out what Powered Now publishes about the devices it supports, which Tuga rugged devices meet the published Android version and which do not, where a Windows tablet fits, and how a UK trade business can buy a single unit to try before buying for the whole team.

Requirements

What Powered Now needs from a device

Each item below comes from Powered Now Ltd's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android: version 14 or newer, devices up to two years old

    The Powered Now help centre says the app is built to run on the latest version of Android and gives the minimum supported Android version as 14, with devices up to two years old supported. Devices on older versions may not work properly. Of the Tuga Android range, the A10 runs Android 14 and the A6 runs Android 15, so both meet the published figure; the A8 runs Android 12, which is below it. The help centre does not say how the two-year device age is measured, so check with the vendor if that matters to you. We could not load the Google Play listing in this check, so the help centre figure is the one used here. Source: support.powerednow.com

  • Unsupported and unofficial devices

    The help centre says Powered Now does not support ColorOS or Huawei devices and does not officially support folding Android devices. None of the Tuga devices is a folding device. The same page says Chromebooks should work but are not tested, and recommends the web version rather than the Android app on them. Source: support.powerednow.com

  • Memory, storage and screen size: 8GB RAM only advised for very large accounts

    The help centre advises at least 8GB of RAM on an iPhone or Android device for very large accounts with many sites. No storage requirement, processor requirement or screen-size requirement is published. For smaller accounts no RAM figure is given. Source: support.powerednow.com

  • Offline: the app works without a signal and syncs later

    The vendor's offline page says the app works without a signal, so you can record information, pictures and signatures related to the job on the smartphone, and create quotes and invoices after a customer visit. It says everything is saved to the cloud as soon as there is a signal, and copied to your other devices and your team. The page lists no offline limitations and no warnings. The vendor's information page adds that quotes, invoices, forms and certificates can be created offline and sync automatically when the connection returns. Source: support.powerednow.com

  • Certificates: Pro tier, with an engineer e-signature set in Settings

    The certificate setup article says certificates are available exclusively on the Pro tier. Each engineer sets a signature under Settings, then Manage Team, using Set Signature and signing in the box, and adds registration numbers in the same area. The site groups forms under Gas, Electrical, Renewable Energy, Plumbing, Oil and Solid Fuel, and other headings. The vendor's information page says there are nearly 100 trade-specific forms and certificates, including gas safety, electrical and risk assessments. Which certificate types you can use depends on your own qualifications and scheme registration, which is a matter for you and your scheme provider. Source: support.powerednow.com

  • Customer signatures: mobile versions only

    A document or project can be signed off by the customer: open the document, open the options menu, choose Sign, have the customer sign in the box and tap save. The help centre says this feature is only available on the mobile versions of Powered Now, so it is a job for the Android app on a tablet or handheld, not for the web version on a Windows tablet. The article does not mention offline use, although the offline page lists signatures as something that works without a signal. Source: support.powerednow.com

  • Photos: device camera, no limits published

    The vendor says jobs can include notes and photos, visible to the office and the field. The App Store listing says you can select and upload multiple images at once from the mobile apps and shows a sync indicator while photos are still uploading. No photo size limit, resolution or camera requirement is published. Source: powerednow.com

  • GPS: optional live staff tracking

    The App Store listing says you can track your employees' location live using GPS, that the feature can be disabled, and that background GPS use can dramatically decrease battery life. The help centre pages we checked publish no GPS hardware requirement. Source: apps.apple.com

  • Windows: web version, Chrome recommended, no published hardware specification

    The help centre recommends Google Chrome for Powered Now Web and says Safari, Firefox and Edge are supported but may be less efficient. It does not mention Windows or macOS versions. The vendor's information page says the software works across iOS, Android, Mac and Windows with data syncing between devices, but publishes no minimum computer specification. Source: support.powerednow.com

Worth knowing. The Tuga A8 is not recommended for Powered Now. It runs Android 12, and the vendor's help centre gives Android 14 as the minimum supported version, so the A8 is below the published figure and the app may not work properly on it. Customer signatures are only available on the mobile versions of Powered Now, so a Windows tablet is not the device for signing off certificates on site. Certificates are available only on the Pro tier, and which certificates you can issue is a matter for your own qualifications and scheme registration, not for the hardware. The vendor publishes no storage, processor or screen-size requirement, and no photo size limit. Live GPS tracking of staff is optional and the vendor warns that background GPS use can dramatically decrease battery life. No barcode, QR or NFC scanning is documented in the pages we checked, so the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine and the W10's optional scanner and UHF RFID reader are not Powered Now features. Powered Now does not name Tuga devices, and we do not describe any device as certified or tested by Powered Now.
Setting up

Getting Powered Now running

  1. Create a Powered Now account at powerednow.com, or ask your account admin to add you as a team member. Certificates need the Pro tier.
  2. On the Tuga A10 or A6, open Google Play and install the Powered Now app, published by Powered Now Ltd. Check the device is on Android 14 or newer in Settings before you install.
  3. Accept the device prompts for the permissions your team uses, such as the camera for job photos and location if your account uses GPS tracking.
  4. In the web version, go to Settings, then Manage Team, and set each engineer's signature and registration numbers so certificates can be issued.
  5. Fit a data SIM so work done offline syncs as soon as there is a signal. Powered Now says everything is saved to the cloud once a signal returns.
  6. Do the office work, such as quotes, invoices and scheduling, in Chrome on a desktop browser. On a Tuga W10, use Chrome.
  7. For the A10, fit the vehicle mounting dock and a 12V car charger so it charges between jobs; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit a tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out on site.
